events.title: US October CPI
events.why_it_matters: Consensus is +0.3% m/m headline (3.9% y/y) and +0.2% m/m core (2.8% y/y); a hot core print would cement the near-fully-priced December Fed hike and pressure rate-sensitive sectors.
events.what_to_watch: Core services ex-shelter and shelter inflation; any upside surprise above 0.3% core.

events.title: China extends suspension of 24% tariff on US imports for two months
events.why_it_matters: Beijing kept the 10% tariff in place but suspended the additional 24% for another two months, averting an immediate escalation and reducing tail risk for exporters and supply chains.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Washington reciprocates with its own suspension extension; any retaliatory signal from USTR.

events.title: Anthropic IPO roadshow begins
events.why_it_matters: The AI lab is targeting a $1.1–1.3T valuation (down from earlier $1.5–2T talk) and a Nasdaq listing before Thanksgiving; pricing will set the tone for the entire AI complex.
events.what_to_watch: Investor demand at the $70–80/share range and whether the deal prices above or below the revised valuation band.

events.title: Russia-US-Ukraine trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi
events.why_it_matters: First face-to-face talks in nine months; any ceasefire progress would weigh on energy prices and lift European risk assets, while failure keeps the war premium intact.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a joint statement or framework is produced; European representation and security-guarantee language.

events.title: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris on Ukraine and Iran
events.why_it_matters: European allies are expected to press Washington on Ukraine and urge restraint on Iran, shaping the diplomatic backdrop for oil and European risk.
events.what_to_watch: Any coordinated statement on Iran or Russia; US Secretary of State Rubio's tone.

events.title: Three oil tankers explode in Strait of Hormuz
events.why_it_matters: The IRGC reported three tankers struck mines in the Strait, briefly spiking oil to around $109 Brent and raising supply-disruption risk for global energy markets.
events.what_to_watch: Whether tanker traffic normalises and whether Iran or the US escalates further; oil price reaction.

events.title: Trump says renewed Iran strikes 'unlikely and unnecessary'
events.why_it_matters: De-escalation rhetoric after the Hormuz tanker incidents reduces the immediate tail risk of a wider military conflict that could disrupt oil flows.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the 'Iron Gate' task force posture changes and whether Iran responds with its own de-escalation.

events.title: US October PPI
events.why_it_matters: Consensus is +0.4% m/m and 6.6% y/y, keeping pipeline inflation uncomfortably high and reinforcing the Fed's hawkish stance.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI and services PPI; any upside surprise above 6.6% y/y.

events.title: US October retail sales
events.why_it_matters: A key read on consumer resilience after strong payrolls; a weak print would contrast with hawkish Fed pricing and complicate the December decision.
events.what_to_watch: Control group sales and discretionary categories; revisions to prior months.

events.title: FOMC October meeting minutes
events.why_it_matters: Minutes will reveal how close the committee was to a December hike and whether any members pushed back, shaping rate expectations into the December 8–9 meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Language on 'further tightening' and the balance of risks; any dissent.

events.title: Fed December hike odds hit 95.6%
events.why_it_matters: Market pricing has moved to near-certainty for a 25bp December hike, leaving little room for a dovish surprise and raising the bar for risk assets.
events.what_to_watch: Whether CPI or PPI can meaningfully shift the odds; Fed speakers before the blackout.

events.title: Nvidia Q3 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: The single most important AI bellwether; guidance will determine whether the recent AI trade drawdown stabilises or deepens across semiconductors and mega-cap tech.
events.what_to_watch: Data-centre revenue, Q4 guidance, gross margins, and any commentary on China export controls.

events.title: Walmart Q3 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Walmart is the best real-time read on the US consumer; slowing comparable sales or cautious guidance would signal holiday-season risk.
events.what_to_watch: US comps, grocery inflation passthrough, and e-commerce growth.

events.title: Target Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Target's discretionary mix makes it a sharper read on consumer stress than Walmart; weak results would reinforce the slowdown narrative.
events.what_to_watch: Apparel and home categories, inventory levels, and margin guidance.

events.title: Baidu Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: A key China internet/AI read; advertising weakness or AI-cloud strength will shape sentiment on China tech.
events.what_to_watch: Core advertising revenue and AI-cloud growth; margin trajectory.

events.title: Tencent Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Tencent is the bellwether for China platform regulation and gaming/AI investment; guidance can move the entire China tech complex.
events.what_to_watch: Gaming revenue, fintech growth, and AI capex commentary.

events.title: Alibaba Q2 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Alibaba's e-commerce and cloud results will show whether China's consumer recovery is holding and whether AI cloud demand is accelerating.
events.what_to_watch: China commerce GMV, cloud growth, and margin trends.

events.title: Cisco Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Cisco is a key enterprise-networking and AI-infrastructure read, often setting the tone for the broader tech hardware complex.
events.what_to_watch: AI infrastructure orders, enterprise demand, and guidance.

events.title: Applied Materials Q4 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Semicap bellwether; orders and guidance will signal whether the AI-driven chip-equipment upcycle is intact.
events.what_to_watch: China revenue exposure, leading-edge spending, and backlog.

events.title: Japan Q3 2026 GDP first preliminary
events.why_it_matters: Consensus is around +1.0% annualised, with weak consumption offset by capex; a soft print could complicate the BOJ's December hike plans.
events.what_to_watch: Private consumption and capex components; whether the annualised rate misses 1%.

events.title: Japan October national CPI
events.why_it_matters: Core CPI is expected near 2.1%; a hot print would reinforce the BOJ's December hike signal and support the yen, pressuring exporters.
events.what_to_watch: Core-core inflation and services CPI; any upside surprise above 2.1%.

events.title: China October industrial production and retail sales
events.why_it_matters: Consensus is for IP around 5.5% y/y but retail sales only around 1.1% y/y, highlighting the persistent consumption gap and need for more stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Retail sales miss and whether IP holds up; any policy response from Beijing.

events.title: PBOC raises FX deposit reserve ratio to 6% effective November 15
events.why_it_matters: The 200bp hike tightens onshore FX liquidity and signals Beijing's discomfort with rapid yuan depreciation, with spillovers to Asian currencies.
events.what_to_watch: USD/CNH reaction and whether the PBOC follows with other liquidity tools.

events.title: Lame-duck Congress faces December 11 shutdown deadline
events.why_it_matters: Republicans must fund the government before December 11 or risk a shutdown; a funding fight in the lame-duck session could inject volatility into year-end markets.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a stopgap is passed or Democrats force concessions; farm bill and defense provisions.

events.title: Supreme Court conference on Nielsen antitrust petition
events.why_it_matters: The justices will consider whether to hear Nielsen's challenge to an antitrust injunction, with potential read-across to platform and data-pricing regulation.
events.what_to_watch: Whether cert is granted and any accompanying statements on tying law.

events.title: LA/Long Beach port strike deadline extended to November 20
events.why_it_matters: A strike by port watchmen at the busiest US container complex would disrupt holiday inventory and freight flows; the third extension pushes the risk to November 20.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a contract is reached before the deadline; any cargo diversion to other ports.

events.title: COP31 climate summit in Antalya
events.why_it_matters: Leaders' summit on November 11–12 will focus on climate finance and implementation; any binding commitments could affect energy and carbon-exposed sectors.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a finance deal emerges and how fossil-fuel language is handled.

events.title: OPEC+ meeting on December output
events.why_it_matters: Just beyond the two-week window, the meeting will review December output after holding steady on November 1; supply signals will matter for oil amid Hormuz risk.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the group signals a pause or a cut; compliance from Iraq and Kazakhstan.

events.title: France social unrest and strike risk
events.why_it_matters: Nationwide strikes and protests over budget cuts disrupted transport and services; continued unrest could weigh on French consumer and industrial activity.
events.what_to_watch: Whether unions call further actions and whether the government concessions hold.

events.title: EU political instability in Belgium and France
events.why_it_matters: Belgium's PM offered to resign over budget talks and France faces fiscal and social strain, feeding euro-area political risk and investor-confidence weakness.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Belgium forms a budget compromise and whether French spreads widen.

top_risks: A hot October CPI print forces the Fed into a December hike with little room for a pause, pressuring rate-sensitive sectors and the AI trade.
Nvidia guidance disappoints or Anthropic IPO prices poorly, triggering a broader AI/semiconductor de-rating.
Iran/Hormuz escalation resumes, spiking oil and tightening global financial conditions.
Russia-Ukraine talks fail, keeping the war premium in energy and European risk assets.
A December 11 US government shutdown fight adds year-end volatility.
top_opportunities: China's two-month extension of the 24% tariff suspension reduces trade-war tail risk and supports exporters and Asian risk assets.
A benign CPI and soft PPI could allow the Fed to signal a pause after December, sparking a relief rally in rate-sensitive sectors.
Nvidia beat-and-raise could reignite the AI infrastructure trade across semis and mega-cap tech.
Anthropic IPO demand could revive AI sentiment if pricing holds at the revised $1.1–1.3T valuation.
Japan CPI/BOJ hike path supports yen and Japanese financials while creating entry points in exporters.
summary: Markets enter November 10 with a near-certain December Fed hike priced in, October CPI due today, and China extending its tariff suspension to reduce near-term trade risk. The next two weeks are dominated by US inflation data, Nvidia and China tech earnings, the Anthropic IPO, and fragile geopolitical talks on Ukraine and Iran. Uncertainty is elevated because a single hot CPI or weak Nvidia guide could swing the AI trade and rate expectations.
